butir.teks: For this reason al-Hasan said, "Two innovators have innovated in Islam: a man of evil opinion who claims that Paradise is for whoever holds an opinion like his, and a man of luxury who worships this world, who is angry for its sake, pleased for its sake, and seeks it. So abandon them both to the Fire."

Indeed, a man who finds himself in this world between a man of luxury who calls him to his worldly life and a man of caprice (hawa) who calls him to his caprice, while Allah Most High has protected him from both of them, yearning for the righteous early generations (salaf), asking about their deeds, following their traces, and placing himself in the way of a great reward: be like that.

It has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud, both as his own statement (mawquf) and with a chain of transmission (musnad), that he said, "There are only two things: speech and guidance. The best speech is the speech of Allah Most High, and the best guidance is the guidance of the Messenger of Allah Most High (peace and blessings be upon him). Beware of newly invented matters, for the worst of matters are the newly invented ones, every newly invented thing is an innovation (bid'a), and every innovation is misguidance. Do not let the time grow long for you, lest your hearts harden. Everything that is coming is near. The far is only what is not coming." (١) And in a sermon of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): "Blessed is he whose own fault keeps him busy from the faults of people, who spends from wealth he earned without disobedience, keeps company with the people of jurisprudence (fiqh) and wisdom, and avoids the people of slips and disobedience. Blessed is he who is humble in himself, whose character is good, whose inner life is sound, and who keeps his evil away from people. Blessed is he who acts upon his knowledge, spends the surplus of his wealth, withholds the surplus of his speech, and to whom the Sunna is ample, so that he does not go beyond it to innovation." (٢) Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say, "Good guidance at the end of time is better than much action." And he said, "You are in a time in which the best of you is the one who hastens in matters, and after you will come a time in which the best of them will be the one who is deliberate and holds back, because of the abundance of doubtful matters (shubuhat)."
He spoke truly. Whoever does not hold back in this time, but agrees with the masses in what they are upon and plunges into what they plunge into, perishes as they perished.

Hudhayfa (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "More astonishing than this is that what you hold to be right today is what was wrong in a time that has passed, and that what you hold to be wrong today is what was right in a time that has come. And you will not cease to be well as long as you know the truth and the scholar among you is not treated with contempt."

He spoke truly, for most of what is held to be right in these times was wrong in the age of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them). Among the foremost things held to be right in our time are adorning mosques and furnishing them richly, spending huge sums on the details of their construction, and spreading fine carpets in them. Spreading mats of reed in the mosque used to be counted an innovation (bid'a), and it was said that it was among the innovations of al-Hajjaj.

The earlier people seldom placed a barrier between themselves and the earth. Likewise, occupying oneself with the finer points of dialectic and disputation is among the most esteemed of the sciences of the people of the time, and they claim that it is among the greatest acts of drawing near to Allah, whereas it used to be among the reprehensible things.
Among these is the use of melodic chanting in the recitation of the Qur'an and in the call to prayer.

Among these too are excessive rigor in cleanliness, obsessive whispering (waswasa) in purification, and assuming remote causes for the impurity of garments, while being lax about whether foods are lawful or forbidden, and the like.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) spoke truly when he said, "Today you are in a time in which caprice (hawa) follows knowledge, and a time will come upon you in which knowledge follows caprice."
Ahmad ibn Hanbal used to say, "They have abandoned knowledge and turned to oddities. How little knowledge they have! And Allah is the One whose help is sought."

Malik ibn Anas (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "People in the past did not ask about these matters as people ask today, and the scholars did not say 'forbidden' or 'lawful'; rather, I found them saying 'recommended' and 'disliked (makruh)'."

Its meaning is that they used to consider the fine points of dislike and recommendation, while as for the forbidden, its foulness was plain. Hisham ibn 'Urwa used to say, "Do not ask them today about what they have newly invented by themselves, for they have prepared an answer for it, but ask them about the Sunna, for they do not know it."

Abu Sulayman ad-Darani (may Allah have mercy on him) used to say, "Whoever is inspired with something good should not act on it until he hears of it in a report (athar), and then he praises Allah Most High if it agrees with what is in his own self." He said this only because the opinions that have been invented have struck the ears and clung to the hearts, and they may cloud the purity of the heart, so that, because of them, a person imagines falsehood to be truth. So he takes precaution in this by seeking support in the testimony of the reports.

For this reason, when Marwan introduced the pulpit into the Eid prayer at the place of prayer, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up to him and said, "Marwan, what is this innovation?" He said, "It is not an innovation. It is better than what you know. The people have become many, and I wanted the voice to reach them." Abu Sa'id said, "By Allah, you will never bring anything better than what I know! And by Allah, I will not pray behind you today." He objected to that only because the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to lean on a bow or a staff, not on a pulpit, in the sermon of the Eid and of the prayer for rain. (١) And in the well-known hadith: "Whoever introduces into our religion what is not part of it, it is rejected." (٢) And in another report: "Whoever deceives my community, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people." It was said, "Messenger of Allah, what is deceiving your community?" He said, "That he invents an innovation and gets people to follow it." (٣) The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has an angel who calls out every day: Whoever opposes the Sunna of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) will not be reached by his intercession." (٤) The likeness of one who wrongs the religion by inventing what opposes the Sunna, compared with one who commits some sin, is the likeness of one who disobeys the king at the heart of his realm, compared with one who opposes his command in a particular service. The latter may be forgiven, but at the heart of the realm, no.
Some of the scholars said, "Silence about what the early generations (salaf) spoke about is rudeness, and speaking about what the early generations were silent about is self-burdening."
Another said, "The truth is heavy. Whoever goes beyond it does wrong, whoever falls short of it is helpless, and whoever stops with it is content."

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Hold to the middle way, to which the one who has gone ahead returns and to which the one who follows behind catches up." (٥) Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, "Misguidance has a sweetness in the hearts of its people." Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 6:70⟧ And Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 35:8⟧ So everything introduced after the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) that goes beyond the measure of necessity and need belongs to play and amusement.

It is related of Iblis (may Allah curse him) that he dispatched his troops in the time of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and they returned to him worn out. He said, "What is the matter with you?" They said, "We have not seen the like of these. We get nothing from them, and they have wearied us." He said, "You cannot overpower them. They kept company with their Prophet and witnessed the revelation of their Lord. But after them will come a people from whom you will get what you need."

If you say, "How did the one who said this know what Iblis said, when he did not see Iblis and Iblis did not tell him that?", then know that the masters of hearts have the secrets of the Dominion (malakut) unveiled to them: at times by way of inspiration, with a thought coming to them as an arrival upon them from where they do not know; at times by way of the true dream; and at times while awake, by way of the disclosure of meanings through the witnessing of images, as happens in sleep. This is the highest of the degrees, and it is among the exalted degrees of prophethood, just as the true dream is one of forty-six parts of prophethood.

So beware lest your share of this knowledge be denial of whatever goes beyond the limit of your own limitation. In that the pretentious scholars perished, who claim that they have encompassed the sciences of the intellect. Ignorance is better than an intellect that calls to the denial of such things in the case of the friends of Allah Most High, and whoever denies this for the friends of Allah is bound to deny the prophets and is outside the religion altogether.

One of the knowers of Allah ('arifun) said, "The abdal withdrew to the ends of the earth and hid from the eyes of the masses only because they cannot bear to look at the scholars of the time, for in their view they are ignorant of Allah Most High, while in their own view and in the view of the ignorant they are scholars."

Sahl at-Tustari (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Among the greatest acts of disobedience are ignorance of one's ignorance, looking to the common people, and listening to the words of the heedless."

Any scholar who has plunged into this world should not be listened to; rather he should be treated with suspicion in everything he says, because every person plunges into what he loves and rejects what does not agree with what he loves. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, ⟦QS 18:28⟧ And the sinning common people are better off in state than those ignorant of the path of religion who believe that they are among the scholars, because the sinning commoner admits his shortcoming, so he seeks forgiveness and repents. But this ignorant one thinks that he is a scholar, and that what he is occupied with, of the sciences that are his means to this world, is enough for him in place of following the path of religion. So he neither repents nor seeks forgiveness, but continues in it until death.

Since this has prevailed over most people, except those whom Allah Most High has protected, and hope of reforming them has been cut off, the safest course for the careful person of religion is seclusion and being alone, away from them, as its explanation will come in the Book of Seclusion, if Allah Most High wills. For this reason Yusuf ibn Asbat wrote to Hudhayfa al-Mar'ashi, "What do you think of one who remains and finds no one with whom to remember Allah Most High except that the person is a sinner or the discussion with him is disobedience? That is because he does not find its people." He spoke truly, for mixing with people is never free of backbiting, or listening to backbiting, or silence over what is wrong, and the best of his states is that he imparts knowledge or receives it. If this poor man were to reflect and know that his imparting of benefit is not free of the blemishes of showing off (riya') and the desire for a following and for leadership, he would know that the one receiving it only wants to make it a tool for seeking this world and a means to evil, so he would be his helper in that, his support, his backer, and the one who prepares its means, like one who sells a sword to highway robbers.

Knowledge is like the sword, and its suitability for good is like the suitability of the sword for fighting. For that reason he is not permitted to sell it to someone whom he knows, from the indications of his circumstances, intends to use it as an aid to highway robbery.

These are twelve signs among the signs of the scholars of the Hereafter, each of which brings together a number of the characteristics of the scholars of the early generations (salaf). So be one of two men: either one characterised by these qualities, or one who admits his shortcoming while acknowledging it. And beware of being the third, deceiving yourself by putting the tool of this world in the place of religion, likening the conduct of the idle to the conduct of the firmly grounded scholars, and joining, through your ignorance and denial, the band of the perishing and despairing.
We seek refuge in Allah from the deceptions of Satan, for by them the masses perished.
